newsitem.title: CHINA: China officials freeze Japan JV golf club assets.
newsitem.headline: China officials freeze Japan JV golf club assets.

text.p: Chinese authorities have frozen the assets of a Japanese joint venture golf club in the southern boomtown of Shenzhen after the club ignored repeated orders to pay outstanding taxes, the China Daily said on Friday.

The Shenzhen taxation bureau had frozen 13 million yuan ($1.57 million) in bank savings as well as the assets of the Honichi Golf Leisure Club, and would auction 10 cars belonging to the club, the newspaper said.

The club's other property would be sealed and put up for auction after it ignored an order last May to pay 70.62 million yuan ($8.5 million) in outstanding taxes as well as a fine of 24.68 million yuan, it said.
The company had been given a payment deadline of April 25.
"However, Honichi still refuses to pay its taxes," the newspaper said.
The golf club had 3,343 domestic and foreign members and received about 977 million yuan in membership fees and cash deposits between 1988 and 1996, it said.
Lured by booming business in southern China and potential fast returns, foreign investors have been flattening hilltops in southern China to build putting greens.
